stumbles.quote: The first round of this experiment measured that 8% and concluded that domain vocabulary does not help much. The second round traced the small saving to the pre-tokenizer.
stumbles.why: Refers to earlier rounds the reader hasn't seen; unclear what differed between rounds, and it sits oddly with the opening 'Yes'.
Oskar is never introduced, so the reader doesn't know who he is or why his question matters.
Names an experiment the text doesn't explain or locate, and it's unclear whether it has been run or what it found.

stumbles.quote: uses 21% fewer tokens than Ettin's tokenizer
stumbles.why: Doesn't say if the comparison is against the 376-token average, and 'cheaper' is never tied to compute or cost. Ettin itself is also never explained.

stumbles.quote: so no published clinical ModernBERT has tried this.
stumbles.why: This is a broad claim that doesn't follow from the two models named. It assumes those are the only clinical ModernBERTs, and the text never explains what they are.

point: Retraining a 50K BPE vocabulary on PubMed abstracts and also switching to whitespace-only pre-tokenization cuts token counts by 21% against Ettin's tokenizer, but keeping GPT-2 pre-tokenization saves only 8%, and whether a model trained on it performs well is untested.
